points.title: Data flow diagram
points.must: Definition: shows how data moves through a system — inputs, processes, data stores and outputs; shows what happens to data, not how or in what order.

points.title: When DFDs are used
points.must: Drawn at analysis (current system) and design (new system); helps analyst, programmers and client agree on IPOS.

points.title: External entity
points.must: Person / organisation / system outside the system that sends data in (source) or receives data out (sink); rectangle; named with a noun; example.

points.title: Process
points.must: Action inside the system that transforms input data into output data; rounded rectangle with a number; verb + noun name; example.

points.title: Data store
points.must: Data held for later use (file, table); open-ended rectangle with ID D1, D2…; noun name; example.

points.title: Data flow
points.must: Data moving between symbols; arrow showing direction; labelled with the name of the data (noun), never an action.

points.title: Drawing of the four symbols
points.must: A labelled sketch of all four Gane–Sarson symbols (or a consistent alternative notation).

points.title: IPOS in a DFD
points.must: Input = flow from entity to process; processing = process; storage = data store; output = flow from process to entity; with an example (e.g. canteen).

points.title: Context diagram
points.must: Level 0: whole system as ONE process with all external entities and flows; shows the boundary; no data stores.

points.title: Level-1 DFD
points.must: Splits the system into its main processes (3–7), adds data stores and flows between processes, stores and entities; processes numbered 1, 2, 3.

points.title: Levels compared
points.must: Table or diagram: context vs level 1 vs level 2 (one process, stores?, numbering 0 / 1,2,3 / 2.1, 2.2).

points.title: Library example
points.must: Sketch or table of the library context diagram and level-1 DFD with entities, processes, stores and named flows.

points.title: Balancing
points.must: Level-1 DFD has the same external entities and the same flows in and out as the context diagram; only adds detail inside.

points.title: How to draw a context diagram
points.must: Steps: one process named after the system, find entities, one labelled arrow per data in/out, check no stores.

points.title: Common mistakes
points.must: Stores on a context diagram; noun-only process names; action words on flows; computer/database drawn as an entity.
